markets-finance.title: India Wants Your Dollars. The RBI Is Dusting Off the 2013 Playbook — NRI Bonds, FCNR Deposits, Emergency Swaps — to Stop the Rupee From Hitting 100. If You Have a Dollar Account, You Are About to Be Courted.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India conducted a $5 billion dollar-rupee swap auction on May 26, 2026 — the same day the rupee was trading near its record low of 96.96 per dollar. But the swap is only one weapon in an escalating arsenal. Sources familiar with the central bank's thinking told multiple outlets that the RBI is actively evaluating the launch of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) deposit schemes, the issuance of NRI bonds, and additional swap operations to mobilise dollar inflows from the Indian diaspora. The last time India took these steps was during the 2013 taper tantrum crisis, when the rupee fell to 68.85 against the dollar and the RBI raised $34 billion from NRIs in three months through FCNR-B deposits offered at subsidised rates. That 2013 operation is widely credited with stabilising the currency and averting a balance-of-payments crisis. India's current predicament is arguably worse: the Iran war has pushed Brent crude above $100 per barrel, foreign portfolio investors have sold $23 billion of Indian equities in 2026, the rupee has fallen 6 percent since January, the RBI is spending an estimated $1 billion per day in the spot market to prevent further collapse, and fuel prices have been hiked four times in May alone — a cumulative increase of ₹7.5 per litre. For the estimated 32 million members of the Indian diaspora — particularly the 4.5 million Indian Americans who hold dollar-denominated savings, earn dollar salaries, and send an estimated $30 billion in remittances to India each year — the coming weeks may present a once-in-a-decade financial decision. The RBI is about to ask you for your dollars. Understanding what FCNR deposits are, how the 2013 scheme worked, what the current remittance and property arbitrage looks like, and whether parking your dollars in India makes financial sense requires more than a headline. It requires context.

sports.image_caption: Virat Kohli during IPL 2026 — the first player to score 600+ runs in four consecutive seasons

sports.excerpt: The head coach has been with CSK since the very beginning, but the team's early exit in IPL 2026 has raised questions. No immediate decision is expected, but the silence from the camp speaks volumes.
sports.image_caption: Stephen Fleming has been Chennai Super Kings' head coach since the franchise's inception.

technology.title: Arvind Krishna's IBM Is Betting $10 Billion That Quantum Computing's Moment Has Arrived
technology.excerpt: The Indian-born CEO is staking a decade of credibility on building the world's first fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029 — with a billion-dollar chip factory to match.
technology.image_caption: Arvind Krishna, CEO of IBM, is leading a $10 billion quantum computing push.
technology.nri_angle: Arvind Krishna joins the rarefied club of Indian-origin CEOs making trillion-dollar technology bets. For Indian quantum researchers and IIT graduates eyeing the field, IBM's commitment signals a new wave of hiring and R&D investment.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: American Airlines and Southwest Are Racing to Double Their India Tech Teams. They're Not Alone.
technology.excerpt: Airlines, retailers, and truck makers are all expanding India technology hubs — a signal that the GCC boom is spreading far beyond banking and Big Tech.
technology.image_caption: Airlines are joining the rush to build technology capability centres in India.
technology.nri_angle: The expansion of GCCs beyond tech and finance into airlines, retail, and manufacturing creates new career pathways for Indian engineers — and a counter-narrative to the AI job-loss fears dominating headlines.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI Is Building an AI Phone. Every App Developer in Bangalore Should Be Paying Attention.
technology.excerpt: The ChatGPT maker is partnering with Qualcomm and MediaTek to build an AI-native smartphone by 2028 — one that replaces apps with agents and could upend the mobile economy India helped build.
technology.image_caption: OpenAI's planned AI-native smartphone aims to replace traditional apps with AI agents.
technology.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs over 15,000 engineers in Hyderabad who may work on the AI phone's silicon. Meanwhile, India's massive app development workforce faces an existential question: if AI agents replace apps, what happens to the millions of developers who build them?
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TSMC Says AI's Biggest Problem Isn't Speed. It's Electricity.
technology.excerpt: The world's largest chipmaker says energy efficiency has overtaken raw computing power as the main constraint shaping future AI chip design — and it's raising prices to match.
technology.image_caption: Server cooling fans in a data centre — energy consumption is now the defining constraint for AI chip design.
technology.nri_angle: Indian chip designers at TSMC, Nvidia, Intel, and AMD are at the forefront of the efficiency shift. India's new fabs in Dholera and Gujarat face the same energy constraints, and the country's power grid makes efficiency-first design a strategic necessity.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Jensen Huang Is Courting Beijing. Nvidia's Chips Keep Showing Up in China Anyway.
technology.excerpt: Nvidia's CEO joins the advisory board of China's most powerful university as Taiwan investigates the smuggling of AI chips through Japan. For Indian engineers and investors, the implications are personal.
technology.image_caption: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, whose balancing act between Washington and Beijing grows more precarious by the week.
technology.nri_angle: Indian engineers at Nvidia face uncertainty as the company navigates US-China tensions. India's semiconductor programme positions the country as a neutral alternative hub — the trillion-dollar question is whether it can build fast enough.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The AI Inference Boom Just Created a CPU Shortage Nobody Predicted
technology.excerpt: ByteDance is building custom processors, Intel and AMD prices are up 35 per cent, and the chip that powered the internet for decades is suddenly the scarcest component in AI.
technology.image_caption: A microprocessor circuit board — CPUs have become the unexpected bottleneck in the AI infrastructure buildout.
technology.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian engineers at Intel, AMD, and ARM are designing the CPUs the world is fighting over. India's bet on RISC-V gains strategic value as ByteDance and others explore the open-source architecture.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Anthropic Refused to Let the Pentagon Use Its AI for Mass Surveillance. Now It's Blacklisted.
technology.excerpt: The standoff between the AI safety company and the U.S. Department of Defense — with a May 31 deadline looming — has become the most consequential AI governance fight in years. Indian AI researchers are watching closely.
technology.nri_angle: Anthropic employs a significant number of Indian-origin AI researchers and engineers, many on H-1B visas, who face direct career uncertainty from the standoff. The case also sets precedent for how AI companies can resist government overreach — a question that matters deeply as India drafts its own AI governance framework. For Indian tech workers choosing between AI labs, the ethics-vs-government-contracts tradeoff just became very real.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Lisa Su Says AI Is 'Still in the Third Inning.' AMD Is Betting $10 Billion on It.
technology.excerpt: AMD's chair and CEO commits the company's largest-ever regional investment to Taiwan's semiconductor ecosystem — and warns the global CPU market is 'tight' with no relief in sight.
technology.nri_angle: AMD's India R&D centers in Hyderabad and Bangalore — with over 6,000 engineers — are deeply involved in EPYC server chip development and AI software optimization. Taiwan's supply chain health directly determines whether those engineers' work reaches production on schedule. For NRI investors, Su's 'third inning' thesis means the AI infrastructure buildout has years of runway left.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nvidia's Vera CPU Is an ARM Chip That Outperforms Intel and AMD. Indian Engineers Helped Build It.
technology.excerpt: The 88-core Olympus processor, purpose-built for agentic AI, has posted benchmark numbers that no ARM chip has ever matched — and thousands of Indian engineers in Bangalore and Pune contributed to its design.
technology.nri_angle: NVIDIA employs thousands of engineers across Bangalore, Pune, and Hyderabad — many of whom contributed to the Vera CPU architecture and its supporting software stack. For Indian chip designers weighing career moves, Vera signals that ARM-based data center processors are no longer a niche bet. And for NRI investors tracking NVIDIA, Vera opens a new $200 billion server CPU market opportunity on top of the GPU business.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Britain Just Told Sunil Mittal He Can't Buy More of BT. Here's Why It Matters.
technology.excerpt: The UK government is blocking India's telecom titan from raising his BT stake beyond 25%, invoking national security over its fibre-optic backbone. For Indian capital eyeing Western infrastructure, the ceiling just got lower.
technology.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal, founder and chairman of Bharti Enterprises. Photo: Wikimedia Commons
technology.nri_angle: Indian billionaire capital being blocked from Western telecom infrastructure raises questions about how Indian investment will be treated globally — relevant to NRI investors, Bharti Airtel shareholders, and anyone watching India's push to become a global business power.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Standard Chartered Is Cutting 7,000 Jobs With AI. Its CEO Called Them 'Lower-Value Human Capital.'
technology.excerpt: The bank plans to eliminate 15% of its back-office roles by 2030, with hubs in Bengaluru and Chennai bearing the heaviest burden. CEO Bill Winters apologised for the phrasing. The layoffs are proceeding anyway.
technology.image_caption: Standard Chartered CEO Bill Winters at the World Economic Forum, 2021. Photo: Wikimedia Commons
technology.nri_angle: Standard Chartered employs tens of thousands in Bengaluru and Chennai back-office hubs — exactly the roles being targeted. For NRI finance professionals and their families in India, this is a direct threat to livelihoods. AI salary inflation of 40-50% in India tech roles means even the survivors face a transformed career landscape.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Synopsys Just Coined the Term 'Agent Engineer.' India's Chip Designers Should Pay Attention.
technology.excerpt: The EDA giant raised its forecast on surging AI chip design demand and struck a deal with activist investor Elliott. Its new pitch: AI 'agent engineers' that work alongside human designers. India's 50,000-strong chip design workforce is directly in the path of this shift.
technology.image_caption: Microchips on a circuit board. AI is reshaping how these are designed. Photo: Pexels
technology.nri_angle: Synopsys employs thousands of engineers in India, its largest non-US engineering hub. India's semiconductor design workforce of ~50,000 engineers is directly affected by the 'agent engineer' concept — AI tools that augment or replace parts of the chip design process. For Indian chip designers in the Bay Area and Bengaluru, this reshapes career trajectories.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Every Bollywood Romance Released in 2026 Has Underperformed. The Genre That Built the Industry Is Running Out of Theatres.
entertainment.excerpt: From 'Chand Mera Dil' to 'Pati Patni Aur Woh Do', not a single romantic film has crossed ₹50 crore this year. For an industry built on love stories, the numbers are a crisis.
entertainment.image_caption: Bollywood romantic films are struggling to fill seats in 2026, as audiences shift to streaming and action spectacles
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Ananya Panday Danced Bharatanatyam in a Bollywood Film. Classical Dancers Called It a Catastrophe. Her Father Said They Missed the Point.

entertainment.image_caption: Ananya Panday's Bharatanatyam-inspired sequence in 'Chand Mera Dil' has divided audiences and classical dance practitioners

entertainment.title: A Song From 2015 Just Became the Most-Streamed Indian Track on Spotify. It Has 717 Million Plays.

entertainment.image_caption: A.R. Rahman composed 'Agar Tum Saath Ho' with an unusual restraint that helped it become the most-streamed Indian song on Spotify

entertainment.title: South Indian Exhibitors Just Mandated an Eight-Week OTT Window. If You Watch Films on Netflix, This Changes Everything.
entertainment.excerpt: The new rule forces all South Indian films to stay off streaming platforms for two full months after theatrical release — a direct challenge to the NRI habit of waiting for OTT.
entertainment.image_caption: South Indian exhibitors have mandated an eight-week gap before films can move to streaming platforms

entertainment.excerpt: The most expensive Telugu film of the year arrives June 4 with Priyanka Chopra's endorsement, Chiranjeevi's intervention in Telangana theaters, and a trailer that hit 175 million views in 48 hours.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Salman Khan Picked Up the Phone on Both Sides of the Don 3 War. Here's What He Said.
entertainment.excerpt: As FWICE's non-cooperation directive against Ranveer Singh divides the industry, Bollywood's most powerful mediator steps in to broker a truce between Singh and Farhan Akhtar.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Drishyam 3 Just Crossed ₹200 Crore Worldwide. Nobody Needed a Third Film. Everybody Watched Anyway.
entertainment.excerpt: Mohanlal's franchise closer becomes the first South Indian film of 2026 to hit $10 million overseas. Kerala led the charge, but it was the Gulf and North America that turned it into history.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Aamir Khan Will Play Lala Amarnath. Rajkumar Hirani Will Direct the 3 Idiots Sequel. Both Films Start Within Months of Each Other.
entertainment.excerpt: Twenty-five years after Lagaan, Aamir reunites with Ashutosh Gowariker for a cricket film rooted in Partition. Then he walks straight into the most anticipated Bollywood sequel in years.

entertainment.title: Beyond the Red Carpet: Indian Cinema Had Its Quietest — and Most Important — Year at Cannes.
entertainment.excerpt: While Aishwarya and Kangana dominated headlines, a student film made official selection from 2,750 entries, a short film screened at Marché du Film, and South Asian storytelling got its first-ever main stage panel.
entertainment.image_caption: The 79th Cannes Film Festival saw quiet but significant Indian cinema milestones beyond the celebrity red carpet

entertainment.image_caption: Desi Bling has become Netflix's most polarizing Indian reality show
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Kattalan Just Opened in Four Languages. It Has a ₹50 Crore Budget, Ravi Basrur's Score, and a Direct Line to Marco.

entertainment.image_caption: Antony Varghese stars as the hunter in Kattalan, Malayalam cinema's latest action thriller
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India's Largest State Just Launched a Wellness Policy to Turn Varanasi and Ayodhya Into Global Ayurveda Hubs. Your Next Trip Home Could Include a Panchakarma Prescription.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Uttar Pradesh's AYUSH Health and Wellness Policy 2026 is India's most ambitious bet on wellness tourism yet. For NRIs spending $3,000 on a weekend spa in Sedona, the same money in Varanasi will get you a month of traditional medicine with a lineage older than Western civilisation.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 463,000 People Found That Loneliness Raises Your Risk of Heart Valve Disease by 23 Per Cent. Living Alone Does Not. The Distinction Matters More Than You Think.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The largest study of its kind found that feeling lonely — not being socially isolated — independently predicts degenerative valve disease. For a diaspora that prizes stoicism and treats loneliness as weakness, the findings are a clinical alarm bell.

sources.label: Journal of the American Heart Association

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: European Cardiologists Now Say Ultra-Processed Food Is a Clinical Risk Factor — Like Smoking. Indian-Americans Eat More of It Every Year They Live Here.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A European Society of Cardiology consensus links UPFs to 65 per cent higher cardiovascular mortality. The traditional Indian kitchen was always the answer.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: The traditional Indian kitchen — dal, sabzi, whole spices — is inherently minimally processed. European cardiologists now say that matters more than calorie counts.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India Just Quarantined a Suspected Ebola Patient in Bengaluru. The US and Canada Have Banned Travellers From Three African Countries. Here Is What Every NRI Needs to Know.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The WHO has declared a global health emergency. India has launched airport screening. If you have family travelling between India and East Africa, the rules changed overnight.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Airport health screening measures have been activated across India and dozens of other countries in response to the Ebola outbreak
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Blood Test Can Now Screen You for Colon Cancer. The American Cancer Society Just Made It Official. South Asian Americans Have the Lowest Screening Rates in the Country.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Guardant Shield test detects tumour DNA in your blood. One in three eligible Americans remain unscreened. For South Asians, that number may be three in four.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A simple blood draw can now screen for colorectal cancer under updated ACS guidelines. | Pexels
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: America Just Declared Your Child's Screen Time a Public Health Crisis. The Recommended Limit for Teenagers Is Two Hours a Day. Most Indian-American Kids Are Doing Double That.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new Surgeon General's advisory calls for bell-to-bell phone bans in schools, age-gated design changes from tech companies, and family media plans. For Indian-American parents who grew up without screens, the rules of engagement just changed.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A 19-Year Study of 20,000 Adults Found That the Type of Sitting Matters More Than the Amount. Mentally Active Sitting Cuts Dementia Risk. Passive Sitting Raises It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers tracked sedentary behaviour for nearly two decades and found that replacing one hour of TV-watching with reading or puzzles was associated with a significant reduction in dementia risk. For Indian tech workers who sit 10 hours a day and come home to Netflix, the distinction is not academic.

sources.label: Frontiers in Public Health — Sedentary Behaviour and Burnout

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Asian Americans Have the Lowest Rate of Anxiety Medication Use in the Country. A National Study of 29,000 Adults Found That Cultural Stigma Is Only Part of the Explanation.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A May 2026 Frontiers study found that even after controlling for income, insurance, and education, Asian adults had 45 per cent lower odds of taking anxiety medication than White adults. For South Asian families where mental health is still discussed in whispers, the treatment gap is likely even wider.

sources.label: Emory University — South Asian Women Mental Health

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 100,000 People Found That Food Dyes Raise Diabetes Risk by 38 Per Cent and Cancer Risk by 14 Per Cent. Your Grandmother's Kitchen Did Not Use a Single One of Them.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The NutriNet-Santé cohort study is the first to link colour additives to chronic disease at scale. Curcumin as an additive — not as turmeric — was the worst offender.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Turmeric in whole-food form offers anti-inflammatory benefits. As an isolated food additive, it was linked to a 49 per cent increase in diabetes risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Diabetes Drug Millions of South Asians Already Take May Be Quietly Slowing Their Cancer. A Cleveland Clinic Study of 12,112 Patients Found the Evidence.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic cut cancer progression by up to 55 per cent across four tumour types. South Asians, who carry the world's highest diabetes burden, may be benefiting without knowing it.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: GLP-1 receptor agonists, originally developed for diabetes, are showing unexpected cancer-protective properties
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 17,000 Adults Found You Need Four Times More Exercise Than the Guidelines Recommend. The 150-Minute Rule Is a Floor, Not a Ceiling.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers at Macao Polytechnic University found that 560 to 610 minutes of weekly aerobic exercise — about 85 minutes a day — reduced cardiovascular events by more than 30 per cent. The standard 150-minute guideline cut risk by only 8 per cent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The American Heart Association Just Rewrote Its Dietary Rules. Your Mother's Indian Kitchen Already Follows Most of Them.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The 2026 AHA guidelines prioritise plant proteins over meat, push potassium and whole grains, and take a harder line on alcohol. Traditional Indian cooking checks nearly every box — except the one about salt.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk
